Planner 01 · Fun
The Stuck
Starter
Games for when you just can't start.
For procrastinators, busy brains and anyone staring at a to-do list that stares back.
This planner belongs to

Start here

How this works

Pick how you feel. Play one page. Start.
I can't start

The task feels like a wall.

Tiny Start Ladder · p4
Too many choices

Everything matters, so nothing happens.

Task Spinner · p5
It's boring

You'd rather reorganize the spice rack.

Roll a Task · p7
It's too big

You don't know where it begins.

Treasure Map · p9
I keep avoiding it

Same task, fourth week running.

Dare Cards · p10
I need a reason

No reward, no motivation.

Scratch & Start · p12

The only rules

  1. Play one page at a time. Not the whole book.
  2. A game picks the task. You start it. No re-rolls unless the pick is impossible right now.
  3. Starting counts. Five messy minutes is a win you can mark.

You don't need to feel ready. You need to begin.

The Stuck Starter

Make the spinner — no scissors needed

  1. Write eight tasks in the list. Keep them all doable today.
  2. Hold a pencil tip upright on the centre dot, through one end of a paperclip.
  3. Flick the paperclip. Where it stops is your task.
  4. Start it within two minutes. Cross it off, spin again later.

Want a fancy one? Cut out the wheel and the arrow on page 6 and join them with a brad.

✂ Make it brad spinner
Too many choices

Spinner parts

Optional: build a spinner that lasts.


Two arrows, in case one goes missing.

Build it

  1. Glue this page to cardstock. Let it dry.
  2. Cut out the wheel and one arrow along the dashed lines.
  3. Poke a hole through the arrow's dot and the wheel's centre with a pen tip.
  4. Push a brad through both. Open its legs at the back. Leave it loose enough to spin.
  5. Write tasks on the numbered wedges in pencil, so you can change them.

Make the scratch squares

  1. Write a small reward in each dashed square (a coffee out, an episode, a nap). Ask a friend to fill them so it's a surprise.
  2. Cover each square with clear packing tape.
  3. Mix 2 parts acrylic paint to 1 part dish soap. Paint two coats over the tape. Let it dry.
  4. Finish the task, then scratch with a coin. Shortcut: use ready-made scratch-off stickers.

The Habit

Small marks. Real change.
For anyone building a habit that sticks: tiny starts, gentle tracking, rewards you actually want, and no guilt when you miss a day.
This planner belongs to

Start here

How this works

The recipe for a habit that lasts.
The habit recipe

After I ,
I will ,
then I'll .

cue → tiny habit → celebrate

1
Make it tiny

Two minutes or less. One push-up. One page.

2
Attach it

Hook it to something you already do every day.

3
Mark it

Fill a dot the moment you do it. Did the tiny version? Write S.

No-guilt rules

  1. Missed days stay blank. They don't erase anything.
  2. Count marks, not streaks. 20 marks in a month is 20 wins.
  3. Stuck? Make it smaller, not harder.

How this works

This planner meets you where you are.
Check your battery

Turn the dial. Be honest — nobody's grading.

Energy menu · p4
Plan a gentle day

Notice small wins

Getting up counts. Eating lunch counts.

Win jar · p7

Gentle rules

  1. Rest is not a reward. You don't have to earn it.
  2. Blank pages are fine. This planner never needs catching up.
  3. If you're struggling a lot, please talk to someone you trust or a professional. This book is a support, not a fix.

Soft is still strong.

The Gentle Reset

3

Punch the card, log it, pull the meter up.

House rules

  1. Every session counts. Five minutes is a session.
  2. Rest days are part of the plan, not a break from it.
  3. Count sessions, not streaks. A missed day erases nothing.
  4. New to exercise, pregnant, or managing an injury or condition? Check with a doctor first.

The best workout is the one you'll actually do.

✂ Make it spinner
Choose

Workout spinner

Can't decide? Spin.

Spin it

  1. Put a pencil tip on the centre dot, through a paperclip.
  2. Flick the paperclip. Do what it lands on for 10 minutes.
  3. Want a sturdier one? Glue to cardstock, cut it out, add an arrow with a brad (see the Maker Guide).

✂ Make it paper die
Choose

Workout die

Six moves. Roll, then do ten.
Roll 1
Roll 2
Roll 3
Roll 4

Make it

  1. Write a move on each face (e.g. 10 squats, 20 jumping jacks, 30-second plank).
  2. Cut out, fold inward, glue the shaded tabs inside.
  3. Roll 3–5 times = a quick workout.

✂ Make it punch card
Mark it

Punch cards

Cut out. Clip to your gym bag or keep in your wallet.

Make it

  1. Print on cardstock and cut along the dashed lines.
  2. Hole-punch (or colour) a circle after every session.
  3. Full card = prize. Tape old cards to page 13 to see them pile up.
